image_description: A close-up portrait of a male Mallard duck (drake) floating on water. The subject features a characteristic iridescent green head, a distinct white neck ring, a yellow bill, and mottled brown/grey chest plumage. The background consists of rippling water with soft focus.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a distinct yellow coloration consistent with a male Mallard.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, contrasting with the green head feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows dense, layered feather texture typical of waterproof plumage. The posture suggests buoyancy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image perfectly matches the Mallard description: iridescent green head, clear white neck ring, and brownish-grey breast feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are submerged or occluded by the body angle and water; they are not visible in this frame.
The wings are folded against the body and largely out of frame or obscured by the angle; only the shoulder area is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail section is outside the frame of this close-up shot.
